name: Judge Dredd
summary: Mega-City One's helmeted street judge, empowered to arrest, sentence and execute on the spot. Created by John Wagner and Carlos Ezquerra for 2000 AD in 1977 to satirise authoritarian policing.
origin: In a dystopian future, the vast Mega-City One covers most of North America's east coast, and police and courts have merged into Judges. Joe Dredd is the most famous of the street judges, who can convict and sentence offenders instantly. John Wagner created him by pushing the tough-cop idea of Dirty Harry to its logical extreme, and the stories use Dredd to satirise authoritarianism and police brutality. His helmet always hides his face except for his mouth and jaw.
powers: Bionic eyes with night vision and reduced blinking
Lawgiver pistol keyed to his palm print, with six ammo types
Lawmaster motorcycle with guns, laser cannon and onboard AI
Daystick, boot knife and stun or gas grenades

storyline.title: From Dread to Dredd
storyline.beat: Pat Mills drops a horror strip called Judge Dread, and Wagner takes the name for his tough-cop concept. A sub-editor tweaks the spelling.

storyline.title: Prog 2
storyline.beat: Ezquerra's launch story is vetoed as too violent. A rewritten script drawn by newcomer Mike McMahon appears in 2000 AD prog 2.

storyline.title: Wagner returns
storyline.beat: Wagner comes back from prog 9 with The Robot Wars, and Dredd becomes the comic's most popular character.

storyline.title: His own title
storyline.beat: Dredd gets his own magazine, the Judge Dredd Megazine.

storyline.title: Stallone's Dredd
storyline.beat: Sylvester Stallone plays him in Judge Dredd, which gets mostly negative reviews.

storyline.title: Dredd
storyline.beat: Karl Urban stars in Dredd, written by Alex Garland, which critics receive much better.

gossip.text: His name comes from Judge Dread, the stage name of British ska and reggae artist Alexander Minto Hughes. Sub-editor Kelvin Gosnell suggested the new spelling.
Wagner gave Ezquerra an advert for Death Race 2000 as visual reference. When he saw the chains and zips Ezquerra added, Wagner first complained it looked like a Spanish pirate.
Ezquerra designed Dredd but didn't draw the first published strip. Accounts differ on why he walked out.
Dredd never takes his helmet off in any adaptation.
gossip.truth: Karl Urban keeps it on throughout Dredd (2012), but Stallone's 1995 film shows his face.

gossip.text: Pat Mills says the name Joseph refers to his old school, St Joseph's College in Ipswich.
Dredd is the longest-running character in 2000 AD.

quiz.q: In which comic did Judge Dredd debut?
quiz.why: He first appeared in 2000 AD prog 2 in 1977.
The Lawgiver only fires for his palm print.

quiz.q: Which city does Judge Dredd police?
quiz.why: Mega-City One covers most of North America's east coast.

theme.tagline: Judge, jury and executioner, all before breakfast.

timeline.title: 2000 AD Prog 2
timeline.note: The helmeted street judge first patrols Mega-City One in the 5 March 1977 issue.

timeline.title: Enter Judge Death
timeline.note: Dredd meets his undead nemesis, a judge from another dimension who outlaws life itself.

timeline.title: Judge Dredd Megazine
timeline.note: Dredd gets a whole magazine of his own alongside his weekly 2000 AD strip.

timeline.title: Stallone's Dredd
timeline.note: Sylvester Stallone takes the helmet off a lot in Judge Dredd, and critics are not kind.

timeline.title: Rebellion takes over
timeline.note: Games studio Rebellion buys 2000 AD and becomes Dredd's publisher.

timeline.title: Dredd
timeline.note: Karl Urban keeps the helmet on in Dredd, which wins over critics and builds a cult following.
